summary.text: Patient 4, a 69-year-old man, was one of nine patients with naïve-treatment active neovascular AMD enrolled in a prospective interventional study at the Department of Ophthalmology, with active CNV confirmed by fluorescein angiography. A baseline complete ophthalmologic examination, SD-OCT and fluorescein angiography were performed, and Table 1 lists baseline visual acuity 20/60 and baseline CRT 453.

After the baseline evaluation (day 0), bevacizumab 1.25 mg/0.05 mL was injected into the vitreous cavity at the same visit, and the patient was instructed to use topical moxifloxacin 0.3% four times daily for 5 days. Daily SD-OCT evaluations were performed for 30 consecutive days after the injection.
Table 1 lists, for this patient, the first day of CRT reduction as 1, the day of minimal CRT as 16 with minimal CRT 361, and the day of maximal CRT as 1 with maximum CRT 453.

Figure 3 OCT B-scans of patient 4 showed an immediate posttreatment decrease of central retinal thickness with a rebound increase of subretinal fluid during follow-up starting at day 18; subretinal fluid recurrence was identified on the 18th day, the final CRT was thinner than at the baseline visit, a slow increase of subretinal fluid continued from day 18 until day 30, and recurrent subretinal fluid was identified on day 30.

article_limitations: Roster numbering follows first mention of individual identity evidence: article patient 4 (Discussion) is p1, patient 8 (Figure 1 caption) is p2, then Table 1 rows in row order; labels keep the article patient numbers.
Table 1 prints no units; the text gives micrometres only for series-level mean CRT values and the figure axes, so table cell units are left null and no unit is added.

All cells are recorded literally and the inconsistencies are kept as ambiguities, not resolved.
The text and captions that name patient 4 and patient 8 are linked to Table 1 rows 4 and 8 only through the shared patient number.

Series-level statements are not copied to individuals: mean CRT values and P values, subgroup means by FA classification, the counts of four predominantly classic and five occult patients (not assigned to patients), the mean number of 27.8 OCT examinations, and the sentence that no ocular or systemic side effects developed during the follow-up period.

The reported mean difference of 206.1 μm does not equal the difference between the reported mean baseline and mean final CRT values; this series-level arithmetic mismatch is not resolved and not a patient fact.

Eligibility criteria (age of 50 years or more, previously untreated active CNV, central macular thickness over 250 μm, VA between 20/25 and 20/400, unremarkable past ocular history) are design criteria and are not recorded as patient facts; the unremarkable past ocular history is not stated for any individual patient.
Figure 2 daily CRT values exist only as plotted lines; no daily value is printed, so none is recorded as a fact (estimated chart readings stay in visual.json).
Which eye was the study eye is not stated; laterality is left unknown.

Methods sentences that do not explicitly cover every patient (pupillary dilation, 30-degree line B-scan with eye tracking, automated segmentation used to assess CRT, exclusion rule) are not copied to individual patients; daily SD-OCT is recorded because the Methods state data were collected daily from all patients.

Figure 2 plotted lines differ from several Table 1 cells (patient 4 minimal CRT; patient 6 minimal and maximum CRT and their days; patient 9 maximum CRT; day of maximal CRT for patients 1, 3, 4 and 5); those cells are review_only with ambiguities. Plotted values stay pixel content.
